guide.intro: Want to replace a handle on an existing cabinet without drilling new holes? The measurement that matters is the distance between the centres of the two screw holes, called hole-to-hole or centre-to-centre.
guide.step1: Unscrew it from the inside of the door or drawer. You can also bring the handle to the store.
guide.step2: Measure, in millimetres, from the centre of one hole to the centre of the other, not the length of the whole handle.
guide.step3: Count the doors and drawers so we can check stock in the finish you chose.
guide.commonBody: Many cabinet handles follow a 32 mm spacing system. These are the common sizes:
guide.diagramLabel: Illustration: a cabinet handle and its two screw holes. The arrow marks the distance between the hole centres, for example 128 mm.
guide.tip: If you get a slightly different number, such as 127 mm, the size is most likely 128 mm. You can also photograph the handle next to a ruler and send it to us on WhatsApp.
